topic.subject: social
topic.title: Natural vegetation and wildlife
topic.scope: tropical evergreen and deciduous forests, thorn forests, mangroves, montane forests, wildlife reserves

misconceptions.statement: Plants grow everywhere on Earth as long as there is soil.
misconceptions.why: Students often ignore the critical role of climate and rainfall in determining plant life.
misconceptions.fix: Vegetation growth is primarily limited by temperature, humidity, and the amount of annual rainfall in a region.

probe.question: Why are there no dense forests in the Thar Desert?
probe.wrong_answer: Because there is no soil in the desert.

misconceptions.statement: All forests are naturally evergreen throughout the year.
misconceptions.why: Common depictions of forests in media and cartoons often show lush green trees regardless of the season.
misconceptions.fix: Many trees shed their leaves during specific seasons to conserve water or survive harsh conditions.

probe.question: Do all trees in India keep their leaves all year round?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because that is what defines a forest.

misconceptions.statement: Tropical deciduous forests are the same as tropical evergreen forests.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate the term 'tropical' and assume all forests in warm regions are identical.
misconceptions.fix: Evergreen forests stay green all year due to high rainfall, while deciduous forests shed leaves to survive dry periods.

probe.question: What is the main difference between evergreen and deciduous forests?
probe.wrong_answer: There is no difference; they are both just tropical forests.

misconceptions.statement: Mangrove forests are found only in deep mountain valleys.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the term 'mangrove' with general forest types and lack knowledge of coastal geography.
misconceptions.fix: Mangroves are specialized plants that grow in coastal areas, specifically in deltas and tidal regions.

probe.question: Where would you typically find mangrove forests?

misconceptions.statement: Wildlife reserves are just zoos where animals are kept in cages.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate the concept of a protected natural habitat with a zoo due to limited exposure to wilderness.
misconceptions.fix: Wildlife reserves are protected natural areas where animals live in their wild, undisturbed habitats.

probe.question: What is the purpose of a wildlife sanctuary?
probe.wrong_answer: To keep animals in cages so people can visit and see them safely.
